title: The $10,000 Terrible Idea
setup: You and your date find a duffel bag in a parking lot containing exactly $10,000 cash, a Polaroid of a llama, and a hotel key card. No ID. You have until midnight to decide what to do.
choices: Try to identify the owner without touching the cash.
Turn it in to police/security immediately.
Keep the cash but investigate the llama/key card mystery.
Leave it exactly where it is and walk away.
complication: At 11:40 p.m. someone texts your phone: “You found Gerald.” Do you answer?
notes: Notice reasoning, not just choice. Does the person revise when new information appears?

title: IKEA Divorce Simulator
setup: You are magically married for 45 minutes. You have an empty apartment, $900, and an IKEA cart. Anything left over pays for dinner.
prompt: Which room do you furnish first, and who gets final veto power?
choices: Bedroom; split veto equally.
Living room; whoever cares most gets veto.
Kitchen; decide by usefulness.
Spend almost nothing and go somewhere ridiculous for dinner.
complication: At checkout, one of you secretly added a completely unnecessary $349 item. What did you sneak in, and does it stay?
notes: Watch how they negotiate disagreement and whether fun is treated as wasteful or valuable.

title: The Accidental Cult
setup: A joke you made together online is misunderstood. Six months later 47,000 people genuinely believe you are spiritual leaders. Followers are outside asking for today’s teaching.
choices: Confess immediately and dismantle it.
Use the platform for something genuinely helpful, then reveal the truth.
Lean into it as performance art.
Disappear and let the legend eat itself.
complication: A follower donates $2 million to the movement, legally and voluntarily. Now what?
notes: Look for what changes when power becomes materially rewarding.

title: The 24-Hour Kingdom
setup: For 24 hours you jointly rule a tiny country of 30,000 people, one beautiful beach, too many goats, and no existing laws. You may create only three laws.
prompt: Choose one serious law, one happiness law, and one ridiculous law.
choices: Protect basic rights; mandatory nap hour; goats get tiny hats.
Universal essentials; public celebration day; ban leaf blowers before 10.
Maximum personal freedom; community feast; politicians must wear sponsor patches.
Create your own three laws.
complication: Citizens overwhelmingly demand a fourth law that both of you hate. Do you allow it?
notes: The follow-up matters more than the first answer: how does the person handle legitimate disagreement?

title: The Ex Museum
setup: Every person you have dated gets one anonymous museum exhibit representing the relationship. No names and no photographs—just one object and a title.
choices: Choose an object representing what you learned.
Choose an object representing what you lost.
Choose an object representing what was absurd about it.
Choose an object representing what you contributed to the mess.
complication: Now create the exhibit representing YOU as somebody else’s ex.
notes: Do they cast themselves only as victim/hero, or can they see their own footprint?

title: The Beautiful Lie
setup: Press a button and you both receive $2 million, legally and tax-free. Somewhere in the world one stranger will permanently believe one harmless false fact of your choosing.
prompt: Do you press it, and what false fact do you choose?
choices: Yes—make the lie delightfully harmless.
No—consent matters even when harm seems tiny.
Yes, but only if we can choose a beneficial lie.
Need more information before deciding.
complication: The stranger is your future child. Same answer?
notes: Compare principle before and after emotional proximity is introduced.

title: The Apocalypse Draft
setup: Civilization moves underground for ten years. Necessities are provided. Each of you may bring five completely nonessential objects. Not people. Not survival gear.
prompt: What five things keep you human?
choices: Comfort objects.
Creative tools.
Entertainment or technology.
Sentimental objects.
complication: Trade lists. Each person must delete one item from the other’s list and replace it.
notes: What they protect after the swap may reveal more than the original five.

title: The Rotating Whale Bed
setup: There is one twelve-foot-wide circular bed. It rotates slowly and plays whale sounds whenever anyone moves. You must both sleep there. One controls lighting; the other controls temperature.
prompt: What is your one additional environmental demand?
choices: Perfect blanket arrangement.
A strict no-touch sleeping zone.
Snacks and water within reach.
Music to drown out the whales.
complication: At 2 a.m. the bed begins rotating twice as fast. Who is fixing this disaster?
notes: Keep interpretation light; this is about negotiating comfort and closeness, not diagnosing sexuality.

title: The Restaurant Inheritance
setup: You inherit a profitable restaurant together. The chef is brilliant and responsible for much of the profit, but is cruel to staff. Replacing him probably cuts profit 30% for a year.
choices: Replace him immediately.
Give one structured chance with consequences.
Keep him and improve protections for staff.
Sell your share rather than run it.
complication: Plot twist: the chef is your brother.
notes: The principle-versus-proximity shift is the key data point.

title: The Tiny Crime
setup: You discover your date has been stealing exactly one plastic spoon from every restaurant they visit for ten years. They have 1,842 spoons arranged beautifully at home.
choices: This is ridiculous; stop doing it.
I hate that I find this charming.
Return or replace the spoons somehow.
I have several logistical questions.
complication: You discover every spoon is labeled with the date and who they ate with.
notes: Useful because the 'wrong' act is trivial enough to expose proportionality rather than obvious morality.

title: The Free House With One Rule
setup: You are given a beautiful paid-off house in your ideal location. You may never change one room. It belongs exactly as the previous owner left it, forever.
choices: Yes; one weird room is worth it.
No; ownership without control isn't ownership.
Only after seeing the room.
Take it and turn the restriction into a ritual.
complication: The room contains hundreds of unopened letters addressed to the previous owner.
notes: Notice how ownership, privacy, and mystery interact.

title: The Wrong Wedding
setup: You arrive dressed up for a wedding and realize neither of you knows the couple. You are at the wrong venue, but everyone assumes you belong and hands you champagne.
prompt: What do you do for the next 20 minutes?
choices: Leave immediately and find the real wedding.
Stay briefly, toast the strangers, then leave.
Commit to the bit and invent a backstory.
Quietly figure out who everyone is before deciding.
complication: The bride asks how you know her mother and hands you the microphone.
notes: Great early-date scenario because playfulness itself becomes visible.

title: The One-Year Fame Button
setup: You can become world-famous for exactly one year for something you choose. After one year, everyone forgets you completely except people who genuinely knew you beforehand.
prompt: Do you press it, and what are you famous for?
choices: Yes—for something meaningful.
Yes—for something absurd and lucrative.
No—fame sounds exhausting.
Yes, but anonymously/masked if allowed.
complication: You learn you cannot profit financially from the fame.
notes: What remains attractive after money is removed?

title: The Memory Trade
setup: You may permanently erase one painful memory, but in exchange you also lose one happy memory chosen at random.
choices: Yes; some pain costs too much.
No; my history is part of me.
Depends which painful memory I can remove.
I would want to know the odds/terms first.
complication: You learn the happy memory lost will involve someone you love.
notes: Avoid treating any answer as pathology; this is about meaning-making and tradeoffs.

title: The Animal Translator
setup: For one day you can understand one species perfectly, but they can also understand everything you say about them.
choices: Dogs.
Crows/ravens.
Whales/dolphins.
Choose your own.
complication: The first thing they tell you is that humans have misunderstood one major thing about them. What do you hope it is?
notes: Pure play with a small window into curiosity and empathy.
